title: ComBodied Agents: a New Paradigm of Human-Centric Agentic AI
task: Human-centered agentic AI for sustained personal support
key_results: Framework integrating software agents, embodied agents, and human services through Personal World Models and admissible intervention policies; proposes scenario-centered evaluation and agency-preservation metrics
comments: Shifts paradigm from task completion to human state modeling, but implementation details and empirical validation are largely conceptual rather than demonstrated.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Single-entity agents cannot match the support quality of systems modeling human state trajectories over time
hypotheses.result: Proposed but not empirically tested in paper

title: Beyond Pixels: From Video Priors to 4D Worlds
task: 4D scene generation from text/image via latent-to-4D synthesis
key_results: Latent-to-4D surpasses Wan+4RC baselines by 2.88–3.45 DINO-F1 points on Text4D-200 and 5.81 on I4D-200; transfers unchanged across multiple video diffusion transformers
comments: Elegant interface design avoiding RGB bottleneck, but evaluation limited to two synthetic benchmarks; human preference results reinforce geometric quality gains.

hypotheses.hypothesis: VAE latent interface enables generator-agnostic 4D prediction without retraining
hypotheses.result: Demonstrated: single checkpoint transfers across Wan, pMF transformers with same VAE family

title: Co-Evolution in Agentic Systems: Toward Self-Directed Evolution Beyond Human Design
task: Taxonomy and evaluation of multi-component self-evolution in agentic systems
key_results: Three-stage taxonomy: Agent–Agent Co-Evolution, Agent–Environment Co-Evolution, and Meta Co-Evolution; identifies open challenges in safety, scalability, and evaluation of increasingly autonomous systems
comments: Survey paper providing conceptual organization rather than new algorithmic contributions; focuses on design space rather than empirical validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Systems that shed human-engineered constraints through meta co-evolution can achieve more robust open-ended improvement
hypotheses.result: Framework proposed; empirical validation deferred to referenced works

title: Articulated Object Reconstruction from Rest-State Observation
task: Articulated object reconstruction from single rest-state image
key_results: Accurate part decomposition and physically plausible articulation from closed configuration without motion observation; competitive with motion-observing and generation-based baselines
comments: Novel ill-posed setting requiring creative integration of vision-language models, segmentation, and video diffusion; but quantitative metrics not explicitly reported.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Articulation hypotheses synthesized by video diffusion can be validated geometrically without ground-truth motion
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: geometric consistency enables joint parameter estimation

title: AdvFD: Boosting Visual Generation via Adversarial Fr'echet Distance Loss
task: Post-training visual generators via adversarial Fréchet distance loss
key_results: AdvFD consistently improves one-step generator post-training across JiT and pMF backbones; addresses Fréchet hacking via learnable adversarial representation with real-feature whitening
comments: Solid technical contribution addressing a real failure mode, but evaluation limited to visual generation metrics without extensive perceptual studies.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Static pretrained feature spaces in FD-Loss enable Fréchet hacking; adaptive adversarial representations prevent it
hypotheses.result: Demonstrated: AdvFD prevents metric stagnation while improving visual quality

title: Mendel Gödel Machine: Recursive Self-Improving Coding Agents via Comparative Evolution
task: Self-improving coding agents via comparative evolutionary principles
key_results: Mendel Gödel Machine (MGM) with reaction-norm mutation and cross-lineage hybridization outperforms single-trajectory baselines; proven faster convergence under additive fitness landscape; confirmed on SWE-bench and Polyglot
comments: Principled application of Mendelian genetics to code generation; theoretical guarantees strengthen empirical claims, though scaling to very large codebases untested.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cross-lineage hybridization and reaction-norm mutation accelerate convergence vs. single-trajectory clonal mutation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: MGM achieves faster and better convergence on benchmark tasks

title: VibeLifeBench: Can Your Life Agent Be Proactive and Persistent in a Living World?
task: Long-horizon proactive LLM agent evaluation in multi-week simulated life scenarios
key_results: VibeLifeBench: 200 tasks across 10 domains in simulated world with autonomous time progression; all frontier models score low (best ~57.3% on easy subsets), exposing gaps in proactivity and constraint inference
comments: Important benchmark exposing real-world limitations; silent world changes and long horizons reveal that prompt-response agents fail at everyday assistance, motivating future work.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Current LLM agents can handle multi-week, multi-constraint, proactive life assistance tasks
hypotheses.result: Rejected: all frontier models score substantially below human (77.3%) performance

title: Ex-Omni-2D: Expressive Omni-Modal Dialogue Models with Native Visual Presence
task: Omni-modal dialogue with coordinated text, speech, and video responses
key_results: Ex-Omni-2D generates personalized video avatars synchronized with speech via shared acoustic-temporal interface; 4-step streaming achieves RTF 1.293 at 400×720/720×400 on 4 GPUs
comments: Novel integration of dialogue, speech, and video generation; acoustic-temporal interface is elegant, but perceptual quality and naturalness evaluation limited to informal description.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Shared acoustic-temporal interface enables learning from heterogeneous dialogue, speech, and avatar data without large-scale multimodal supervision
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: model trained without query–text–speech–video quadruples

title: Decoding-Level Taboo: A Diagnostic Stress Test for LLM Robustness
task: Stress-test LLM robustness by forcing off-nominal generation paths via logit-space intervention
key_results: Decoding-Level Taboo reveals that off-path robustness correlates with model scale and instruction alignment; larger, better-aligned models recover better from forced circumlocution
comments: Clever diagnostic tool exposing deployment–benchmark divergence; results suggest alignment mitigates off-path brittleness, but causal mechanisms remain opaque.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Off-nominal robustness is primarily determined by parameter scale and post-training alignment
hypotheses.result: Confirmed across open-weight model families

title: SkillZip: Evaluation-Free Skill Compression for Self-Evolving Agents by Discovering Reusable Structure
task: Evaluation-free compression of accumulated self-evolution skills into reusable structures
key_results: SkillZip compresses bloated skills via typed minimum description-length objective; one-shot and continual Zip-on-Write modes enable efficient updates without rollouts or replays
comments: Addresses practical skill bloat in self-evolving agents; formalization as MDL over skill contracts is principled, but evaluation on real agent skill libraries limited.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Structural explanation can compress skills without evaluation-guided rollouts
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: one-shot and continual modes achieve compression while preserving coverage

title: SPIEval: Evaluating Large Language Models as Mobile Assistants over Scattered Personal Information
task: Evaluating LLM mobile assistants on scattered personal information integration
key_results: SPIEval: 250 tasks across 10 apps, 4,335 records; best model (GPT-5.5) achieves 57.3%, worst 16.4%; 79% failures due to inaccurate information localization; <2% use advanced search
comments: Well-grounded benchmark exposing real gaps in LLM information retrieval and disambiguation; preference inference and multi-intent decomposition are harder than expected.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Current LLMs can reliably localize information across fragmented personal data sources
hypotheses.result: Rejected: 79% of failures stem from localization errors

title: Not Worth Another Token: Marginal Value Estimation for Efficient Deep Research Agents
task: Context pruning for efficient long-horizon research agents via marginal value estimation
key_results: Early pruning yields largest end-to-end token savings (73% reduction); lightweight heuristics competitive with learned pruning; pruning location more important than scoring rule
comments: Practical guidance for production research agents; finding that early pruning dominates has immediate deployment value, though trade-offs between quality and latency vary by task.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Early-stage pruning (pre-retrieval) yields larger savings than late-stage (pre-synthesis)
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: early pruning dramatically reduces token cost without quality loss

title: InSight-doc: Agentic Visual Perception for Long-Document Understanding
task: Adaptive visual resolution for efficient long-document reasoning
key_results: InSight-doc: selective zooming reduces hallucination >40% and latency 41–68% on long documents while maintaining accuracy lead; 17.9K SFT + 19.2K RL examples improve baseline 4.3–16.4 points
comments: Elegant reasoning-time resource allocation; agent learns when to zoom without external retriever, but evaluation limited to document VQA; generalization to other document types unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive resolution zooming reduces inference cost and hallucination vs. fixed high-resolution processing
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: >40% hallucination reduction and 41–68% latency savings

title: Reference-Free Post-Training of Open Large Language Models for Multilingual Machine Translation
task: Reference-free post-training of multilingual translation via policy optimization
key_results: MiLMMT-46-v1.0 improves SFT baseline across 46 languages via GRPO with reference-free quality estimation; outperforms Seed-X, HY-MT2, TranslateGemma; matches proprietary systems (Google Translate, Gemini 3 Pro, GPT-5)
comments: Strong engineering effort combining GRPO and checkpoint interpolation; reference-free reward signals enable scaling to 46 language pairs, though no explicit ablation on reward composition.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Reference-free reward models enable competitive multilingual MT without human-curated references
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: GRPO with quality estimation achieves leading scores across 46 languages

title: UniMoMo: Expert Merging-Based MoE Acceleration for Large Recommendation Models
task: Expert merging-based MoE compression for recommendation models without online modules
key_results: UniMoMo: post-training compression via functional similarity; four-expert checkpoints achieve 99.92–102.30% NDCG@10 of source with 1.28–1.63× speedup; two-expert achieves 98.36–104.24% with 1.47–2.21× speedup
comments: Clever functional similarity metric avoids parameter distance pitfalls; layer-adaptive protection prevents high-traffic expert merging, preserving critical routing paths.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Functional similarity-based merging preserves recommendation quality better than parameter-distance approaches
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: <1% NDCG loss even at aggressive 2-expert budgets

title: DistilVDR: A Compact End-to-End Visual Document Retriever via Dual-Student Distillation
task: Compact end-to-end visual document retrieval via bilateral distillation
key_results: DistilVDR-524M: 61.74 avg NDCG@5 on ViDoRe (86.9% of 8B teacher); 15.6× smaller index than multi-vector baseline; 10× faster indexing
comments: Elegant asymmetric encoder design (70M query, visual-heavy document) with strong distillation results; pointwise cosine loss avoids contrastive terms, reducing training complexity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Bilateral distillation from frozen teacher embedding space enables efficient single-vector VDR without relevance labels
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 524M student matches 86.9% of 8B teacher quality

title: 360CityArena: A Realistic Virtual Urban Navigation Benchmark for Embodied Agents
task: Embodied agent navigation and spatial reasoning in photorealistic urban environments
key_results: 360CityArena: 175 tasks in Akihabara (602 360° video segments, 85 streets); humans 77.3%, Gemini 2.5 Flash 17.1%, exposing vast urban navigation gap
comments: High-quality photorealistic benchmark revealing that even frontier VLM agents struggle with realistic city-scale navigation; useful for future embodied AI development.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Current frontier agents can perform urban navigation and spatial reasoning at human level
hypotheses.result: Rejected: 17.1% vs. 77.3% human performance

title: iFAN: Inference-Aware Learning for Plain Mask Transformers
task: Inference-aligned training for mask transformer segmentation
key_results: iFAN: Adjusted Probability-Mask Ranking + Cross-Layer Self-Distillation improve panoptic by 1.20 PQ, instance by 1.30 AP, semantic by 0.63 mIoU with negligible overhead
comments: Solid incremental improvement addressing a real training–inference mismatch; distillation between layers is well-motivated, though gains are modest and architecture-agnostic claims need broader validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Explicit optimization of query competition and cross-layer knowledge transfer improves inference quality
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: consistent gains across COCO, ADE20K, Cityscapes

title: DSAgentBench: Can Agents Automate End-to-End Data-Science Workflows in Real Computer Environments?
task: Autonomous data-science workflow execution in real computer environments
key_results: DSAgentBench: 275 tasks spanning full data-science lifecycle in real environments; best model (Claude-4.6-Sonnet) 56.70%, open-source <1%; failures in tool orchestration, OS grounding, multi-step reasoning
comments: Important benchmark capturing true end-to-end complexity; real environment grounding and multi-tool coordination expose gaps that synthetic task simulators miss.

inputs: tool APIs (notebooks, IDE, terminal, browser, DB)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Current agents can automate full data-science workflows in realistic computer environments
hypotheses.result: Rejected: substantial capability gap remains; only 56.7% success for best closed-source, <1% for open-source

title: TSDS-Toolbox: A Toolbox for Measuring Time-Series Dataset Similarity
task: Unified framework for measuring and comparing time-series dataset similarity methods
key_results: TSDS-Toolbox: systematic reproducible comparisons, extensible architecture for custom datasets/methods/tasks, evaluation of dataset-level and series-level similarity methods
comments: Useful infrastructure contribution for time-series research; limited novel algorithmic insights, but addresses fragmentation in similarity benchmarking.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Unified framework enables fair comparison of heterogeneous time-series dataset similarity methods
hypotheses.result: Framework proposed and validated on diverse settings

title: JigShape: Evaluating Visual-Geometric Reasoning in VLMs through Jigsaw Puzzles
task: Evaluating VLM geometric reasoning via jigsaw puzzle solving with interlocking pieces
key_results: JigShape: 95K instances (4×4 to 16×16 grids); frontier models fail at zero-shot on 4×4 (only GPT-4.5 >random); all models collapse on larger grids (''scaling cliff''), <5% on 12×12
comments: Elegant benchmark exposing geometric reasoning limitations; tab-and-blank constraints eliminate texture ambiguity, but focus on jigsaw puzzles may not reflect real-world geometric tasks.

hypotheses.hypothesis: VLMs can maintain geometric constraint satisfaction as puzzle complexity increases
hypotheses.result: Rejected: severe scaling cliff observed across all models

title: Power law graph attention: exact generalization of scaled dot-product attention, empirical collapse at inference
task: Theoretical analysis and empirical validation of Power Law Graph Attention in LLMs
key_results: PLGA generalizes scaled dot-product attention (SDPA) via learned input-generated bilinear operator; inference-collapse theorem shows exact input invariance collapses to generalized SDPA; measured inference fluctuations 10^−6; machine-checked proofs in Lean 4
comments: Highly technical paper mixing theory (Perron-Frobenius structure, NOTEARS regularization) with empirical measurements; claims are rigorously stated but practical impact on model performance unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Power law bilinear operators in attention preserve relative-position dependence under nonresonance conditions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: commutant criterion identifies structure-preserving operators

hypotheses.hypothesis: Exact input invariance of outputs leads to inference collapse to constant SDPA
hypotheses.result: Proven as inference-collapse theorem

title: Glucose-responsive probiotics for glycaemic modulation in mice and monkeys
task: Engineer oral-deliverable glucose-sensing probiotics for autonomous diabetic glycemic control
key_results: Engineered probiotics demonstrated efficacy in multiple diabetic mouse and non-human primate models with improved lipid profiles and attenuated diabetic complications following long-term oral administration
comments: Transient intestinal residence of probiotics may limit sustained therapeutic effect; safety profile for engineered live organisms requires careful long-term monitoring despite avoiding transplantation concerns.

inputs: blood glucose levels above normal threshold

hypotheses.hypothesis: Glucose-responsive HexR-based transcriptional regulator can enable sense-and-respond control of transgene expression in intestinal probiotics
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; probiotics showed glucose-responsive therapeutic dosing in vivo

hypotheses.hypothesis: Oral-deliverable probiotics can achieve long-term metabolic benefits comparable to transplanted cell therapies without surgical risks
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; demonstrated efficacy in mouse and non-human primate diabetic models with improved lipid profiles

title: Meloxicam protects against muscle and metabolic decline in ageing through Cdon restoration and oxidative stress modulation
task: Identify Cdon as driver of muscle aging and test meloxicam efficacy in restoring muscle function
key_results: Cdon expression declines with aging and sarcopenia; meloxicam induced Cdon expression and increased muscle mass/function in young mice; meloxicam mitigated age-related atrophy via Ampk-dependent restoration of redox balance and mitochondrial metabolism
comments: The identification of Cdon decline as a conserved hallmark of muscle aging is noteworthy, and the mechanistic link through Ampk-Cdon-Nrf2 redox axis is well-supported, though in vivo translation to human sarcopenia requires clinical validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cdon decline is a hallmark of muscle aging; meloxicam preserves muscle integrity by restoring redox and metabolic homeostasis through Ampk-dependent maintenance of Cdon
hypotheses.result: Meloxicam induced Cdon expression and improved muscle mass/function in aged mice via Ampk activation and redox balance restoration

title: NUPR1 inhibition prevents mitotic catastrophe: a novel therapeutic strategy for podocyte injury in diabetic kidney disease
task: Prevent mitotic catastrophe in diabetic kidney disease podocytes
key_results: NUPR1 inhibition suppressed Cyclin B2 expression and preserved podocyte numbers; ZZW-115 treatment significantly reduced albuminuria in DKD mice
comments: The NUPR1-BRD2/Cyclin B2 axis provides a mechanistically clear therapeutic target, though translating this to human therapeutics will require safety profiling of NUPR1 inhibitors.

hypotheses.hypothesis: NUPR1 promotes aberrant G2/M phase entry via NUPR1-BRD2/Cyclin B2 transcriptional complex
hypotheses.result: Genetic/pharmacological disruption of NUPR1-BRD2 interaction suppressed Cyclin B2 and prevented MC

title: Pharmacological SOS1 inhibitor BI-3406 synergizes with BCR::ABL1 TKIs reducing leukemia stem cells and overcoming imatinib resistance in CML
task: Evaluate SOS1 inhibition synergy with BCR::ABL1 TKIs to overcome imatinib resistance in CML
key_results: BI-3406+imatinib significantly prolonged survival in p210BCR/ABL mice, reduced LSK/HSPC populations, and restored TKI sensitivity in imatinib-resistant patient samples; mechanism involves RAS/RAC-ERK/AKT pathway suppression
comments: The restoration of TKI sensitivity in clinically resistant patient samples is therapeutically promising, though the incomplete understanding of SLC22A4-independent mechanisms limits full mechanistic clarity.

model_io.model: p210BCR/ABL transgenic mice treated with BI-3406±imatinib
Human CML cell lines and primary patient-derived bone-marrow cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: SOS1 inhibition synergizes with BCR-ABL TKIs by attenuating RAS/RAC signaling and impairing LSC self-renewal
hypotheses.result: BI-3406+imatinib combination suppressed proliferation, increased apoptosis, and restored TKI sensitivity in resistant samples

title: SNAI1 ablation alters integrin-mediated adhesion and endocytic fate
task: Determine SNAI1-FOXA1 transcriptional mechanism regulating integrin adhesion and endocytic fate
key_results: SNAI1 knockout downregulates integrin-based adhesion and endocytic components via FOXA1 derepression; FOXA1 represses ARF6/PSD4 and integrin/MMP genes; SNAI1 knockout cells show defective adhesion, invadopodia, FAK/SRC signaling, and reduced EV uptake/secretion
comments: The elegant SNAI1-FOXA1-ARF6/PSD4 axis elegantly links EMT regulation with vesicular trafficking and EV biology, though the precise role of this axis in tumor progression versus suppression remains context-dependent.

model_io.model: SNAI1 knockout triple-negative breast cancer cells
SNAI1 knockout cells with ARF6/PSD4/FOXA1 manipulation

outputs: integrin and endocytic gene expression changes

hypotheses.hypothesis: SNAI1 represses FOXA1 to maintain expression of ARF6/PSD4 and integrin/MMP genes, coordinating cell plasticity with adhesion and EV secretion
hypotheses.result: SNAI1 knockout cells showed FOXA1-dependent downregulation of ARF6/PSD4 and integrin genes, resulting in defective adhesion, invadopodia, and EV trafficking

title: Concomitant ablation of SOS1 and SOS2 triggers a lethal phenotype involving compromised intestinal integrity and widespread septicemia
task: Determine role of SOS1/SOS2 in intestinal homeostasis and sepsis resistance
key_results: SOS1/SOS2 double-knockout mice exhibited gut-derived lethal bacteremia, intestinal barrier breakdown, and immune cell depletion; stemness enhancement improved survival
comments: This work reveals SOS1/SOS2 as critical for intestinal stem cell maintenance, though the mechanistic link between RAS signaling and epithelial regeneration capacity could be more thoroughly explored.

model_io.model: SOS1/SOS2 DKO mice with stemness enhancement therapy

hypotheses.hypothesis: SOS1 and SOS2 are required for intestinal stem cell maintenance and barrier integrity during systemic infection
hypotheses.result: Combined genetic ablation triggered sepsis-like pathology; therapeutic stemness reinforcement restored survival and tissue organization

title: Photostimulation improves maturation of human photoreceptors
task: Determine whether rhythmic light flickering enhances photoreceptor maturation in retinal organoids
key_results: Rhythmic light flickering at specific frequency improved outer segment formation, promoted transcriptional shifts toward mature photoreceptor states, and enhanced responsiveness of downstream retinal neurons
comments: The use of patterned light as a non-invasive developmental stimulus is elegant and physiologically relevant, representing a significant improvement over dark culture conditions for retinal organoid maturation.

model_io.model: Human retinal organoids with rhythmic light stimulation
inputs: rhythmic light flickering at specific frequency

hypotheses.hypothesis: Patterned light is a potent physiologically relevant signal for driving retinal organoid differentiation and photoreceptor maturation
hypotheses.result: Rhythmic light flickering enhanced outer segment formation, promoted mature photoreceptor transcriptional states, and improved downstream neuron responsiveness

title: Human in vitro skeletal muscle models recapitulate age-related atrophy and contractile decline induced by aged serum
task: Model age-related skeletal muscle atrophy in vitro and test quercetin efficacy
key_results: Aged serum reduced MF20+ cell area by ~40% in 2D model and decreased contractile force in 3D model; quercetin suppressed NF-κB activation and mitigated atrophy
comments: This human in vitro system successfully recapitulates aging-induced atrophy, providing a valuable screening platform, though it remains unclear if quercetin's effects translate to systemic interventions.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Aged serum induces muscle atrophy via NF-κB-mediated upregulation of E3 ubiquitin ligases
hypotheses.result: Quercetin suppressed NF-κB activation and mitigated aged serum-induced atrophy and contractile dysfunction

title: Hesperetin activates the Hmgcs2-Pparα-Cisd2 signaling axis and delays liver aging
task: Identify signaling pathways regulating liver aging and test hesperetin efficacy
key_results: Hesperetin restored Cisd2 expression, improved liver pathology, and reversed aging-associated transcriptomic alterations; Hmgcs2-Pparα-Cisd2 axis is largely responsible for protective effects
comments: The identification of a single molecular axis (Hmgcs2-Pparα-Cisd2) as a major regulator of liver aging is elegant, though the specificity and sufficiency of this pathway for systemic aging remain to be fully validated.

model_io.model: Naturally aged mice treated with hesperetin

outputs: PPARα and CISD2 expression by age

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hmgcs2 interacts with Pparα to activate Cisd2 transcription through PPRE elements
hypotheses.result: Genetic/pharmacological validation confirmed Cisd2-dependent protective effects of hesperetin

title: Rb-driven transcription limits its tumour-suppressive effects in breast cancer
task: Elucidate how pharmacologically activated Rb remodels chromatin and influences ER-driven transcription in HR+ breast cancer
key_results: CDK4/6 inhibition redistributes hypophosphorylated Rb to ER-rich transcriptional hubs, enhancing ER target gene expression in an Rb-dependent manner; KDM5A interaction with Rb mediates this pro-proliferative program
comments: This work reveals a previously unappreciated pro-growth activity of Rb that limits CDK4/6 inhibitor efficacy in endocrine-resistant cancers, representing an important mechanism of acquired resistance.

model_io.model: HR+ breast cancer cell lines treated with CDK4/6 inhibitors

hypotheses.hypothesis: CDK4/6 inhibition-activated Rb integrates into ER-rich hubs via KDM5A interaction, promoting pro-proliferative ER target gene expression
hypotheses.result: Rb-dependent enhancement of ER target genes persists in endocrine-resistant settings, limiting CDK4/6 inhibitor efficacy

title: Luminescent-reaction-enabled super-resolution imaging
task: Develop chemistry-enabled super-resolution imaging using luminescent reactions
key_results: RIED framework achieved ~100 nm super-resolution for ECL, CL, BL imaging of intracellular organelles; enabled 41-hour continuous live-cell imaging of mitochondrial transfer dynamics with high sensitivity
comments: The laser-free super-resolution approach offers unique advantages for live-cell imaging and extreme temporal resolution, though photon budget limitations and potential phototoxicity of chemical reactions require careful optimization.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Spatiotemporal recording of luminescent-reaction-driven photons combined with entropy-weighted correlation and deconvolution enables super-resolution imaging
hypotheses.result: RIED achieved ~100 nm resolution for ECL, CL, BL imaging and enabled ultralong-term continuous super-resolution live-cell imaging

title: Brønsted-basic small molecules activate GTP hydrolysis in KRAS-Q61 mutants
task: Develop small molecules that accelerate GTP hydrolysis in KRAS-Q61 mutants as therapeutic approach
key_results: Brønsted-basic compounds enhanced GTP hydrolysis in KRAS-Q61X mutants up to 20-fold by introducing general base into active site; compounds reduced GTP-bound RAS and suppressed downstream signaling in mutant cancer cells
comments: This chemical strategy of compensating for the loss of Gln61 is innovative and mechanistically elegant, though selectivity for Q61 mutants over wild-type KRAS and specificity for tumor cells require further optimization.

Mutant cancer cell lines with KRAS-Q61 mutations

hypotheses.hypothesis: Small-molecule Brønsted-basic compounds compensate for loss of catalytic Gln61 by introducing general base, selectively enhancing GTP hydrolysis in KRAS-Q61 mutants
hypotheses.result: Compounds achieved up to 20-fold enhancement of GTP hydrolysis and suppressed downstream signaling in mutant cancer cells

title: Structural and molecular principles of DAMP biology
task: Survey structural and molecular principles of DAMP-mediated immune signaling
key_results: Comprehensive framework integrating DAMP release mechanisms (gasdermin, MLKL, NINJ1), receptor sensing (TLR4, P2X7, AGER, STING1), and downstream signaling through assembly-driven mechanisms
comments: This is a review paper synthesizing current DAMP biology; while comprehensive, it highlights mechanistic gaps in understanding precise conformational states that determine immunogenicity.

title: Effects of berberine on ferroptosis and osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs under high-glucose conditions: association with the Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 signaling pathway
task: Investigate berberine effects on ferroptosis and osteogenic differentiation in BMSCs under high glucose
key_results: BBR dose-dependently inhibited high-glucose-induced ferroptosis and promoted osteogenic differentiation via Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 pathway activation; Nrf2 inhibition partially reversed anti-ferroptotic effects
comments: The dual pro-osteogenic and anti-ferroptotic effects suggest berberine targets a common upstream mechanism, though whether this pathway translates to improved bone regeneration in vivo remains to be demonstrated.

hypotheses.result: BBR dose-dependently suppressed ferroptosis while enhancing osteogenic markers; Nrf2 inhibitor co-treatment partially reversed anti-ferroptotic effects

title: Branched-chain α-ketoacid dehydrogenase activation reveals divergent sphingolipid and adipokine responses in adipocytes differentiated from visceral adipose-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (ADMSCs)
task: Characterize heterogeneous metabolic responses to BCKDH activation in adipocytes
key_results: Responder adipocytes showed increased ceramide/sphingomyelin and decreased adipokine secretion with elevated Akt/GSK3 phosphorylation; non-responders exhibited opposite effects and enhanced mTORC1 signaling
comments: The identification of responder and non-responder phenotypes highlights important individual metabolic heterogeneity, though the functional implications for obesity and metabolic disease remain to be established.

hypotheses.hypothesis: BCKDH activation via BT2 treatment produces divergent sphingolipid and adipokine responses based on intrinsic metabolic adaptation capacity

title: The placenta significantly limits fetal glucocorticoid exposure and undergoes cell-specific transcriptomic remodeling in response to maternal stress in mice
task: Determine placental mechanisms limiting fetal glucocorticoid exposure during prenatal stress
key_results: <5% of maternal corticosterone reached the fetus; 14-22% was metabolized; ABCA2 identified as potential corticosterone efflux regulator; stress-induced transcriptional remodeling confirmed by single-nucleus and bulk RNA-seq
comments: This work importantly shifts the paradigm of fetal programming from direct glucocorticoid transfer to placental barrier function, though direct validation of ABCA2's role in corticosterone transport remains incomplete.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The placenta strongly restricts maternal corticosterone transfer to the fetus, limiting direct fetal glucocorticoid exposure during prenatal stress
hypotheses.result: <5% corticosterone transfer with 14-22% placental metabolism; indirect placental responses likely more important for fetal programming

title: Deciphering the platinum resistance heterogeneity landscape of Ovarian cancer through integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data
task: Characterize platinum resistance heterogeneity in ovarian cancer and identify therapeutic targets
key_results: Nebo classification model identified 12 hub genes in highly resistant malignant cells; SPINT2 knockdown sensitized OV cells to cisplatin by reducing RAD51 stability and inhibiting homologous recombination repair
comments: The multi-algorithm integration for platinum resistance scoring is methodologically rigorous, though the mechanism by which SPINT2 regulates RAD51 stability requires further mechanistic validation.

title: Long-term daily light exposure boosts human retinal organoid differentiation
task: Determine whether daily light exposure enhances differentiation and maturation of retinal organoids
key_results: Six hours daily light starting from day 70 in vitro accelerated differentiation of late-born cell types, especially rod photoreceptors, without increased stress or cell death
comments: Light conditioning of retinal organoids is a simple and physiologically relevant approach to enhance maturation, though the specific light-responsive genes and pathways driving this acceleration remain to be elucidated.

title: A frog bioactive peptide suppresses inflammation by modulating autophagy for skin wound regeneration
task: Characterize wound healing mechanism of amphibian peptide OL-RA11 via autophagy and Wnt signaling
key_results: OL-RA11 enhanced autophagy in macrophages promoting M2 polarization and inflammation resolution; simultaneously activated Wnt pathway in keratinocytes enhancing migration and re-epithelialization
comments: The elegant cell-type-specific dual mechanism is well-characterized, though the identity of the direct molecular target(s) of OL-RA11 remains unknown, limiting structure-activity relationship development.

title: Three-dimensional mapping of intact ovaries reveals the aging dynamics of the ovarian reserve
task: Quantitatively map oocyte dynamics across reproductive lifespan using 3D imaging and mathematical modeling
key_results: Mapped >85,000 oocytes in whole ovaries; newly activated oocytes represent fixed fraction of total pool despite age-related decline; oocytes enriched along lateral axis; bimodal size distribution suggests developmental bottleneck
